title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Bhutan: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Bhutan: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Bhutan: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: When a family member faces a serious or terminal illness in Bhutan, care and administrative planning involve public referral hospitals under the Ministry of Health, legal representation and will formalities under the Judiciary of Bhutan, and retirement or provident fund rules at the NPPF [1] [3] [4] [7]. We set out five practical steps so families can arrange medical support, powers of attorney, pension nominees, wills, and land or document records in good time [2] [3] [6].

steps.title: Coordinate hospital, palliative, and home care
steps.html:
• Connect with public referral and palliative teams: Under the Ministry of Health of Bhutan, basic public health services are provided free to Bhutanese citizens through Dzongkhag hospitals and tertiary centers led by Jigme Dorji Wangchuck National Referral Hospital (JDWNRH) in Thimphu, which coordinates specialized medical, nursing, and home-based palliative support [1] [2] [10].
  • Keep clinical records and referrals aligned: Maintain the patient's medical referral book, citizenship ID (CID) number, and outpatient file cleanly between local hospitals and JDWNRH, and confirm ward contact numbers (+975 2 322496 or +975 2 325244 at JDWNRH) [2].
  • Clarify decision-making communication: Because standalone advance-directive statutes do not operate separately in Bhutan, speak directly with attending specialists about prognosis, pain-control choices, and which family member acts as primary contact [1] [10].

steps.title: Arrange formal representation and Power of Attorney early
steps.html:
• Authorize a proxy before capacity declines: Under Section 148 of the Civil and Criminal Procedure Code of Bhutan 2001, an adult party lacking physical or mental capacity may be represented by a family member, legal guardian, holder of a Power of Attorney over business affairs, or a licensed Jabmi (advocate under the Jabmi Act) [4] [5].
  • Observe written agreement and stamp rules: Under Section 35 of the Evidence Act of Bhutan 2005, written authorizations and agreements are legally valid when made in the presence of one witness for each party, signed by all parties or a duly empowered representative, and executed with a legal stamp [3].
  • Check bank-specific mandate forms: Financial institutions such as Bank of Bhutan often ask for notarized or witnessed bank mandates alongside a general Power of Attorney if a caregiver manages pension or household accounts [3] [4].

steps.title: Review NPPF pension, provident fund, and nominee records
steps.html:
• Verify NPPF membership and nominations: Civil servants, armed forces staff, and participating corporate employees should contact the National Pension and Provident Fund (NPPF) (toll-free 1039 or WhatsApp 17170884) to verify Pension (Tier 1) and Provident Fund (Tier 2) beneficiary nominations and pension savings bank details [7] [8].
  • Note retirement and early-pension rules: Under NPPF eligibility rules, monthly pensions commence after 23 years of membership upon reaching normal retirement age (or up to five years early with actuarial reduction), while Surviving Family Benefits cover eligible spouses, up to three children under 18, or surviving parents [7].
  • Keep authorized contact details current: Inform NPPF of any change in mobile number, pension savings account letter, or authorized representative [7] [8].

steps.title: Draft a valid will and organize land records
steps.html:
• Execute a written will under Chapter VII: Under Section Ga 7-2 of the Inheritance Act of Bhutan 1980, a capable person making a will should list all immovable property (land and houses) and movable assets, specify proportions, sign alongside witnesses, and present the will before a Court of Law (Royal Court of Justice / Dzongkhag Court) [6].
  • Note rules on oral wills and non-citizen spouses: Only where a written will is impossible may an oral declaration before two witnesses be written and signed within 30 days (Sections Ga 7-3 and Ga 7-11), and Section Ga 6-23 restricts non-Bhutanese spouses/children without citizenship to inheriting movable property only [6].
  • Verify thram records via eSakor: Check household census and land ownership entries through the National Land Commission Secretariat (NLCS eSakor portal) (+975-02-325170) so property titles match civil records [11].

steps.title: Prepare documents if cross-border recognition is needed
steps.html: • Attestation for international use: Per the HCCH status table, Bhutan is not a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention [9]. Any Bhutanese power of attorney, medical certificate, or court document needed abroad must be notarized by a Public Notary Office and attested by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and External Trade (Department of Protocol and Consular Affairs; Nu. 300 fee, non-laminated originals) before destination embassy legalization [12].

prefillQuestion: A family member is facing a serious or terminal illness in Bhutan. We need an overview of the main official steps and contacts in Bhutan for palliative care, powers of attorney, advance directives, and caregiver support.

contacts.name: Ministry of Health of Bhutan
contacts.note: Oversees universal free public healthcare delivery, Dzongkhag hospitals, and national palliative care planning.

contacts.name: Jigme Dorji Wangchuck National Referral Hospital (JDWNRH)
contacts.note: Bhutan's apex referral hospital in Thimphu (+975 2 322496 / 325244 / 325384) providing oncology, palliative, and specialized inpatient care.

contacts.name: National Pension and Provident Fund (NPPF)
contacts.note: Toll-free 1039 (WhatsApp 17170884) handles member pension and provident fund nominations, authorizations, and Surviving Family Benefits.

contacts.name: Royal Court of Justice
contacts.note: Dzongkhag and Thromde Courts receive written wills under the Inheritance Act 1980 and oversee legal representation and guardianship petitions.
